findings.charge: The subject asserts that CLAUDE-LRLJ-V1-SF1 'Landed in this lineage at leftover-join.v4.' It landed at leftover-join.v2. The repair the finding demanded - replacing the imported DR-119 SATISFIED token on registerRow DR-G14 with DR-G14's own token - is fully present in v2, together with the two other carriers the disposition names. v3 and v4 carried that repair forward without changing it. The attribution is wrong by two generations, in the one field whose job is to record the custody of a finding whose own charge was misstated register custody.
evidence: leftover-join.v1 (a41c529f...) carries file08StatusToken 'SATISFIED Class B (D-091); G14 not QUALIFIED' and has no registerRowNote. That is the defect CLAUDE-LRLJ-V1-SF1 charged: 'file08StatusToken imported DR-119 SATISFIED onto registerRow DR-G14' (v1 review 7169d88d..., verdict REJECT).

leftover-join.v2 (87f8b2a0...) carries file08StatusToken 'OPEN', introduces registerRowNote, retains leftoverDesignOpenStanding, and declares lands: ['CLAUDE-LRLJ-V1-SF1']. Its findingDisposition entry is {id: CLAUDE-LRLJ-V1-SF1, severity: SHOULD-FIX, disposition: 'ACCEPTED', landedAt: ['file08StatusToken','registerRowNote','leftoverDesignOpenStanding']}. That is the landing, and it is v2.

leftover-join.v3 (25d31840...) and leftover-join.v4 (301904f0...) each carry file08StatusToken 'OPEN', lands: ['CLAUDE-LRLJ-V1-SF1'], and a findingDisposition entry byte-identical to v2's - same id, same severity, same bare 'ACCEPTED', same three landedAt carriers. Nothing distinguishes v4 as a landing site; it is the third carrier, not the first.

The subject's own landedAt list ['file08StatusToken','registerRowNote','leftoverDesignOpenStanding'] is byte-identical to v2's. The subject therefore names v2's carrier set while attributing the landing to v4.

On-point precedent, same dispatcher, adjacent lineage: CLAUDE-PTLJ-V7-SF1 (SHOULD-FIX, produced a REJECT of platform-tcb-leftover-join.v7) reads 'v7 newly asserts that CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 Landed in this lineage at leftover-join.v6. It landed at leftover-join.v5. The sentence is a v7-introduced, unfounded custody attribution in the very field that records the custody of a finding whose own charge was misstated lineage custody.' platform-tcb-leftover-join.v8 and v9 both repaired to 'leftover-join.v5' and were accepted.

Second on-point precedent, and it is this subject's own last heading: CODEX-LQLJ-V4-SF1 charged language-quality-leftover-join.v4 with 'First landing of CLAUDE-LQLJ-V1-SF1 and LQLJ-V1-SF1 is leftover-join.v2. leftover-join.v3 carried the repair forward. leftover-join.v4 misattributed first landing to leftover-join.v3.' That produced a Dual REJECT. language-quality-leftover-join.v5 repaired the sentence to 'ACCEPTED. Landed in this lineage at leftover-join.v2. leftover-join.v3 carried the repair forward. This v5 does not re-land it.' and was recorded Dual ACCEPT 0/0 at D-273 - the very decision this v6 remasures against, and the artifact this v6 cites as the current DR-118 leftover-join.

Why this survived D-260: the v5 Stage A review recorded 'landingConfirmedAtV4: leftover-join.v4 carries lands and file08StatusToken OPEN. The landing is real and belongs to v4.' That confirms a sufficient condition - v4 carries the repair - and mistakes it for the first landing. It never opened v2 or v3. The v5 acceptance is therefore not evidence that the attribution is founded; it is an instance of confirming rather than refuting, which this dispatch forbids.

The misattribution is v5-introduced. v2, v3, and v4 all carry the bare disposition 'ACCEPTED' with no landing-version sentence at all. v5 was the first artifact in this lineage to name a version, and it named the wrong one. v6 reproduces the sentence verbatim except for the speaker label.
